calls.head: The Hurricanes should drive the play
calls.body: The Hurricanes have been one of the league’s best at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Jets near the bottom. Expect the Hurricanes to spend more of the night in the Jets’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Hurricanes make it seven straight
paras: The second period was a wild one. Mark Scheifele opened the scoring for the Jets early in the period. Mark Jankowski tied it 1-1 for Carolina on the power play just under four minutes later, his sixth straight game with a goal. Alex Iafallo restored the Jets’ lead less than three minutes later, but they didn’t score again. Jesperi Kotkaniemi tied it up for Carolina late in the second, and Nikolaj Ehlers put the Hurricanes ahead for good on the power play early in the third.

The Hurricanes outshot the Jets 37-23, but the Jets’ looks were better, so the chances came out about even. Pyotr Kochetkov made 21 saves for the Hurricanes, and Clay Stevenson stopped 34 of 37 at the other end. Kochetkov has won all five of his starts this season. The Canes improved to 7-1-1, still first in the NHL in points percentage, while the Jets dropped to 4-2-2, fourth in the Central.

items.text: The Hurricanes are rolling: seven straight wins.
Mark Scheifele has a point in five straight games.
The Hurricanes have beaten the Jets four straight times, going back to the 2024-25 season.
With Jordan Staal out, Jankowski took his spot and scored.
